title: Collector Observability & Chaos Test Plan for Evidence Pipeline
body:
Purpose and scope

This doc specifies an end-to-end observability and chaos-testing plan for the evidence collection pipeline used by our control-evidence tooling. It complements the collector runtime contract by describing what telemetry, metrics, logs, and SIEM export shapes we require, plus a runnable set of chaos experiments and acceptance criteria. The goal is to ensure collector behavior remains correct and debuggable under real-world failures and to validate automated backfill/repair paths.

Audience
- Security engineers responsible for evidence integrity and retention
- Platform engineers who operate the collector fleet
- SREs and test engineers implementing chaos runs and synthetic traffic
- Solutions engineers integrating SIEM exports

High-level objectives
- Define minimal observability surface for every collector instance so incidents are actionable within 10 minutes.
- Validate collector idempotency and checkpointed resumes under failures (crash, network partition, partial writes).
- Verify SIEM export mapping and schema stability for compliance audits.
- Prove backfill path can recover 100k items/hour with <1% lost or duplicated evidence in bounded windows.

Non-goals
- This is not a full ingestion performance benchmark for production (separate load tests cover that).
- Not prescribing specific DB vendors or SIEM vendors; mappings are generic.

Telemetry and signals (required)
- Metrics (time-series, prometheus format preferred):
  - collector.uptime_seconds: monotonic uptime per instance
  - collector.evidence_ingested_total{type, tenant}: cumulative count of evidence items accepted
  - collector.evidence_exported_total{destination, tenant}: successful exports to downstream (SIEM / archive)
  - collector.ingest_latency_ms{p50,p90,p99}: end-to-end latency from event arrival to durable store/ack
  - collector.export_latency_ms: latency to push to SIEM/export sink
  - collector.checkpoint_lag_seconds: time since last durable checkpoint commit
  - collector.kv_cache_hits / collector.kv_cache_misses: cache effectiveness for prefix dedupe
  - collector.retry_backoff_count: number of retries for transient errors
  - collector.error_rate{code} : errors per minute by failure code (validation, storage, network)
  - collector.duplicate_rate: detected duplicates per 1000 items

- Logs (structured JSON, enrich with labels): each log line must include time, level, instance_id, shard_id, tenant, request_id, correlation_id, event: {type}, and minimal payload (e.g., evidence_id or batch_id). Example fields:
  - timestamp
  - instance_id
  - collector_version
  - tenant_id
  - shard
  - evidence_id
  - evidence_type
  - capture_status: received | validated | stored | exported | backfilled | failed
  - bytes
  - error_code
  - checkpoint_seq
  - checksum_sha256

- Traces: instrument long-running flows (validation -> store -> export) with a trace id that maps back to log correlation_id. Capture spans for: validation, encryption, storage_write, export_push, checkpoint_commit.

SIEM export schema (required mapping)
- Destination index/event must contain the following canonical fields (flat key names):
  - event_time (RFC3339)
  - evidence_id (string)
  - evidence_type (string)
  - collector_id (string)
  - tenant_id (string)
  - capture_status (string)
  - source_host (string)
  - original_source (string) // e.g., k8s-audit, osquery, cloudtrail
  - rbac_actor (string)
  - rbac_role (string)
  - correlation_id (string)
  - checksum (hex)
  - export_status (string)
  - processing_latency_ms (number)
  - sequence_number (number) // monotonic per-collector partition
- Provide a smallAvro/JSON schema used for export; any missing required fields must be rejected at the collector (with helpful error_code).

Runtime contract expectations (collector behavior)
- Exactly-once semantics best-effort via a combination of dedupe by checksum + sequence numbers + idempotent storage APIs.
- Checkpointing interval default: 30s or 500 items, whichever first. This value is configurable per-tenant.
- Partial writes must be detectable. Every stored evidence record must include a write-commit marker and checksum. If a marker is absent, record is considered incomplete and scheduled for backfill.
- Backfill must be idempotent and include a provenance envelope referencing original capture attempt(s).

Failure modes and detection rules
- Crash/restart: collector should resume from last committed checkpoint; collector.checkpoint_lag_seconds spiking indicates recovery problem.
- Network partition to SIEM: export queue should persist on disk (bounded queue) and export_latency_ms will rise; metric collector.export_queue_depth should be added in future.
- Clock drift: if local clock jumps, sequence numbers + monotonic timestamps are used. Collector must attach both local_time and monotonic_offset to every record for reconciliation.
- Partial batch failure: if some items in a batch fail validation, collector must emit per-item failure logs and continue with others.

Chaos test matrix (runnable experiments)
- Environment: staging cluster that mirrors production topology with at least 3 shards and 5 collector replicas. Generators simulate tenants with mixed evidence rates.

1) Pod kill during checkpoint commit
  - Action: kill one collector pod while checkpoint commit is in flight (use sleep to time it).
  - Expected: other replica(s) pick up shard; restarted pod resumes from last committed checkpoint; no items lost beyond in-flight window (<= checkpoint interval).
  - Metrics to watch: collector.checkpoint_lag_seconds, collector.evidence_ingested_total delta, duplicate_rate.
  - Acceptance: lost_or_unrecoverable_items = 0; duplicates <= 0.5% for the window.

2) Network partition to SIEM endpoint
  - Action: block egress to SIEM for 5–20 minutes, allow local ingestion to continue at normal rate.
  - Expected: collector persists export queue; evidence_exported_total stalls, export_latency_ms increases; when network restored, drain backfill without duplicates or data loss.
  - Acceptance: queued items persisted across restart; final export success for >=99.5% of queued items.

3) High ingestion spike + disk pressure
  - Action: generate 10x normal ingestion for 15 minutes while reducing available ephemeral disk by 40% on one shard node.
  - Expected: collector enforces backpressure (rejects with 429 and proper error codes) when queue thresholds hit, emits metric collector.reject_rate, and operators can apply autoscale.
  - Acceptance: no silent writes/failures; rejections are explicit and logged with actionable messages.

4) Corrupted checksum inserted upstream (malformed payload)
  - Action: send payloads with incorrect checksum and mismatched schema fields.
  - Expected: collector rejects with validation error, logs details, metric collector.error_rate increment, no corrupt data stored.
  - Acceptance: corruption detection rate = 100%; incidents within 10 minutes have root cause statement in logs.

5) RBAC enforcement regression test
  - Action: run synthetic captures with actors of various roles (admin, auditor, read-only-service, compromised-service). Some requests should be rejected by RBAC v2 policy.
  - Expected: policy decisions logged (rbac_actor, rbac_role, decision, policy_id) and audits exported to SIEM.
  - Acceptance: rejected requests are denied consistently and produce an audit entry exported within retention SLA.

Test harness and automation guidance
- Tests should be implemented as reproducible pipeline runs under ./tests/collector-chaos in the repo (linked artifact above). Each experiment must:
  - spin up synthetic tenant generators (rate + variance parameters),
  - orchestrate chaos (kubectl + tc/netem rules),
  - capture prometheus snapshots pre/during/post,
  - aggregate and assert metrics via a CI-run test runner (pytest or go test harness).
- Use canary shards to limit blast radius; tag all staging telemetry with test_run_id so results are isolated.

Acceptance criteria (summary)
- Observability: critical troubleshooting fields present in >=99% of logs and traces.
- Recovery: no evidence loss for crash/restart within checkpoint window.
- Backfill: ability to replay 100k items/hour with final duplication <=1% and no missing items.
- SIEM exports: exported events match canonical schema; missing required fields cause rejection at collector.

Operational runbook (quick steps during incidents)
1) Identify affected shards via collector.checkpoint_lag_seconds and export backlog metrics.
2) Check logs for last checkpoint_seq and correlation_ids for a sample of missing evidence.
3) If network to SIEM is down, enable disk-backed queue policy and scale export workers; start controlled drain once restored.
4) For partial writes, mark shard for backfill and run backfill job with test_run_id; monitor for duplicates.

Backfill/repair notes
- Backfill must annotate records with backfill_attempt_id and original_capture_ts.
- Repair jobs must be idempotent: they should use sequence_number + checksum to dedupe before write.
- Maintain proofchain links: when backfilled, emit a provenance event to SIEM linking original attempt and backfill token.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Add exporter_queue_depth metric: currently planned but not implemented; prioritize for next sprint (ENG-3145).
- Decide default checkpoint interval per-tenant SLA tiers.
- Schema versioning strategy for SIEM exports: semver of schema vs schema_id in payload?

References and artifacts
- Runtime contract PR: github.com/redwood-inference/evidence-collector-runtime/pull/142
- Related runbooks: confluence:collector-runtime-observability-v1
- Test repo: github.com/redwood-inference/tests/collector-chaos

Checklist before merging to main
- [ ] Confirm metric names with SRE metrics guild
- [ ] Add exporter_queue_depth metric to runtime
- [ ] Create templated Prometheus dashboards for the metrics above
- [ ] Implement structured log schema enforcement in collector
- [ ] Add automated chaos tests to CI with gating thresholds

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: the required fields and tests are minimal but focused on high-impact failure modes. Suggest we iterate after the first two chaos runs (expected in staging next week).
